messages.content:
The failing test `testSingleOptionSingleArgument` in `BugCLI158Test` class creates a default value parser using the `createDefaultValueParser` method with defaults set to `["100", "1000"]`. It then sets the entered value to `"1"`, creates command line arguments `["-b", "1"]`, parses them using the parser, and retrieves the values for the option `-b`.

The current bug report describes a behavior where default arguments only work if no arguments are submitted. The expectation is that for 1 or 2 arguments passed in, the values should be set accordingly without using the default values.

By looking at the `createDefaultValueParser` method, it sets the default values for the option `-b` with a minimum of 0 and a maximum of the length of the defaults array. This means that when no arguments are passed, the default values `["100", "1000"]` will be used.

To address the issue described in the bug report, the logic in the `createDefaultValueParser` method needs to be adjusted to handle the case where arguments are passed in and override the default values accordingly.

The steps to diagnose and fix the issue are as follows:
1. Update the `createDefaultValueParser` method to handle arguments passed in and set the values accordingly without relying solely on default values.
2. Modify the logic in the `createDefaultValueParser` method to consider passed arguments before applying default values to ensure the expected behavior of options with arguments.

The method to be fixed:
```java
org.apache.commons.cli2.bug.BugCLI158Test.createDefaultValueParser(java.lang.String[])
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
